gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SIRUI's own US store sells the Traveler 7C carbon kit for $149.90 today, with a 8 kg / 17.6 lb maker-rated load, 1,665 mm / 65.55 in maximum height and 1.57 kg weight. That is below ChatGPT's $159.95 'best value' aluminum Befree and less than half of the $399.95 Peak Design price.
standout_why: I compared against Finding the Universe (cited, updated 2026-11-08). It lists nine tripods, including the Peak Design Carbon and Aluminium, Vanguard Vesta GO 204CB, Vanguard VEO 3T 204ABP, Manfrotto Befree GT XPRO, SIRUI AM-284, K&F Concept Ultralight Carbon, JOBY GorillaPod 5K and Gitzo Traveler Series 1. The Gitzo (about £540) is the only one with a price. The page has no SIRUI Traveler model and no US prices. ChatGPT's own answer covers only two Manfrotto Befree kits and the two Peak Design tripods. Digital Camera World (cited) would not load past its title through WebFetch, and curl was not approved, so I could not check its list. That is why the score is 2 and not 3.
decides: The SIRUI Traveler 7C becomes the value DSLR pick. Its maker-rated load, maximum height and price all beat the aluminum Befree ChatGPT called 'best value'. It loses to the Befree Advanced carbon (1.25 kg, 410 mm closed) and the Peak Design carbon (2.8 lb per Finding the Universe) on weight, and its 480 mm folded height is the longest in this set. The SIRUI Traveler 5C we already list should not be the DSLR pick. Its maker-rated load is 4 kg / 8.8 lb and its maximum height is 1,380 mm / 54.3 in, half the load of the 7C or the Befree Advanced carbon. It suits a mirrorless kit or a light DSLR with a short lens.
